details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for severe storms capable of mainly damaging wind gusts is expected to increase late this afternoon into evening. A severe thunderstorm watch is likely

details.label: Discussion
details.text: In the wake of an MCV moving from south-central into southeast PA, clouds are gradually clearing, allowing for increased diabatic heating this afternoon. When coupled with a moist boundary layer characterized by boundary-layer dewpoints in the upper 60s to mid 70s F, latest objective analysis indicates MLCAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg with decreasing convective inhibition. Additional air mass destabilization is expected through the remainder of the afternoon, allowing ongoing QLCSs to spread east into the discussion area. Damaging wind gusts will be the primary hazard with the most intense storms, especially in the vicinity of any embedded bowing structures that may persist. A brief tornado or two is possible in areas that can maintain more of a southerly wind component, where low-level shear is locally enhanced

details.label: Watch probability

details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated thunderstorms are forecast to evolve southeastward out of the Black Hills through this evening. The primary hazards will be isolated large hail and damaging wind gusts

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Convective development is ongoing across portions the Black Hills in southwestern South Dakota and adjacent areas of Montana/Wyoming. Expectation is for at least an isolated thunderstorm or two to eventually evolve southeastward out of the Black Hills. While available buoyancy remains weak as of 1900 UTC, further insolation should result in additional destabilization through the afternoon to around 1000-1500 J/kg MLCAPE. Effective shear of 30-40 kts and steepening mid-level lapse rates may promote a supercell or two capable of isolated large hail, with steep low-level lapse rates and the possibility of eventual clustering also supporting a risk for occasional damaging/severe wind gusts. Current expectations are for thunderstorm/severe coverage to remain too isolated for watch issuance; however, a targeted Severe Thunderstorm Watch could be considered should convective coverage/severe risk trend greater than anticipated

details.label: Summary
details.text: Widely scattered thunderstorms will develop along the Colorado Front Range and Raton Mesa vicinity this afternoon, bringing a risk for large hail and damaging wind gusts to portions of the central High Plains

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Aided by strong diurnal heating and easterly, upslope flow with dewpoints near 60 F, widely scattered thunderstorm formation is expected this afternoon along the CO Front Range and Raton Mesa vicinity of the central High Plains, with some lightning activity already noted within deeper updrafts as of 1830 UTC. Around 1500 J/kg MLCAPE (increasing to 2000 J/kg locally by peak heating this afternoon) and 25-35+ kts of effective shear amid modestly strong westerly flow aloft will aid in the organization of updrafts and should support at least a couple of supercells. These storms will pose a risk for primarily large hail owing to the presence of steep mid-level lapse rates exceeding 7-7.5 C/km, with a few damaging/severe wind gusts also possible. A more outflow-dominant/cluster storm mode, and proportionally greater damaging/severe wind gust risk, should be increasingly favored with southward extent as objective analysis indicates effective shear decreases to 20-25 kts across southeastern Colorado and areas farther south. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch may be needed for at least a portion of the discussion area to cover these threats

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for mainly damaging wind gusts is expected to spread east across the watch area through the remainder of the afternoon

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A QLCS with two distinct bowing segments has evolved over eastern OH as of 1815Z, with the TCMH terminal Doppler radar indicating outbound velocities up to 60 kt in the 0.5-1 kft layer near and east of Zanesville. Decreasing clouds downstream from the QLCS over western PA will support further destabilization, allowing the convective system to continue east through the remainder of the afternoon. The ILN VWP has shown a steady increase in westerly winds in the 1-6 km AGL layer since late morning, which will sustain the ongoing bowing structures and related, organized cold pools. As such, expect the threat for damaging winds to progressively spread east across the watch area this afternoon, particularly in the vicinity of the embedded bows. Around 30 kt of 0-3 km shear oriented largely perpendicular to the QLCS may support some brief tornado potential, especially near and north of the apexes of the bows. Farther south, a separate line segment has evolved over northwest WV within a similar environment, suggesting a damaging wind risk with that activity as well
